transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-10-14 10:00 PDT | Duration: ~60m | Attendees: Lena Park, Marco Ruiz (Redwood) + Sarah, Tom, Priya (BlueNova)

Summary: Quick internal enablement to tighten messaging and rehearse a 12-minute demo set. Focus on how to position Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private, answer common latency/cost Qs, and surface security talking points.

Topics: messaging, demo flow, competitive rebuttals, security appendix, next steps

[00:00:00] Lena: Hi everyone, thanks for joining, we'll run about 60 minutes. Marco and I will run through the script, practice the demo, call out where we want to insert benchmarks and competitive notes.
[00:00:22] Marco: Yep, quick note — we're aiming for a tight 12-min demo segment, then 20 for Q&A / roleplay. I'll open the demo and we can time it.
[00:00:38] Sarah: Sounds good. I want to make sure we hit the security piece — customers always ask SOC2, encryption, and KMS flow.
[00:00:52] Lena: absolutely, we'll keep a 2-minute 'security elevator' section. Also rehearsal on the private deployment pitch.
[00:01:10] Marco: Alright starting script. Intro: "Redwood is a developer-first inference platform" — we say: hosted API, dedicated reserved capacity, and private VPC/on-prem options.
[00:01:30] Marco: (mumble) sometimes I say 'Redwood dedicated' like 'Redwood dedicates' — don't do that.
[00:01:40] Lena: ha, noted. Quick competitive framing: we call out that OpenAI is great for general purpose hosted but we differentiate on predictable capacity and private deployment. Anthropic gets mentioned for safety, and Vertex for cloud integration.
[00:02:05] Tom: For the demo script, when do you mention batching and KV cache? Customers ask how you reduce token cost without blowing latency.
[00:02:20] Marco: Good Q. We have a mid-demo callout after the scoring example — we say: "we use KV cache + prefix caching to reduce per-token work, and we have intelligent batching policies that don't violate latency SLOs."
[00:02:45] Sarah: And you have numbers for that? Like percent improvement?
[00:02:52] Marco: We should mention typical numbers: 30-50% token cost reduction on repeat prefixes, 10-40% throughput gains with smarter batching. But call this 'workload dependent' and offer to run a quick benchmark.
[00:03:12] Lena: action item: Marco will add a slide with 30% ballpark caching improvement and a footnote.
[00:03:28] Marco: Moving to the demo — I'll share screen, start the inference console.
[00:03:40] [00:03:40] Marco: (typing noises) Ok, console up. Navigation: model catalog, stream demo, embeddings endpoint, logs. I open a text generation route and start a 3-shot prompt.
[00:04:05] Priya: quick note, keep the UI flow simple, customers get lost in too many tabs.
[00:04:14] Marco: yep, we'll stick to 2-3 screens. Starting generation now — show streaming, you can see tokens come in.
[00:04:35] [00:04:35] Marco: (demo audio) response arrives in ~120ms from warmed instance — we'll mark that as "warmed latency" example.
[00:04:52] Sarah: 120ms is great. How do you explain cold start?
[00:05:00] Marco: Cold start depends on model size, quantization, and whether KV cache warmed. For dedicated pools cold start is rare; for hosted we have warm pools but cold paths exist. We say: "cold start may be 2-6s for large models, but warmed responses are sub-200ms typical for short contexts."
[00:05:22] Lena: Insert benchmark slide here — Marco to record a short clip of cold vs warm.
[00:05:31] Tom: Customers care about SLA and fallback — what do we say when capacity is constrained?
[00:05:40] Marco: Smart routing and automated fallbacks — policy based routing by latency/cost/region, automatic fallback to compatible model variants. We have a 'graceful degradation' narrative.
[00:06:00] Lena: Ok now let's role-play a tough question: "Why not just use OpenAI and be done?" Marco, you want to take it.
[00:06:12] Marco: Sure. Response: "OpenAI is a strong hosted option for general access, but Redwood provides predictable throughput and deployment flexibility — you can get reserved capacity, VPC/private deployment for data residency and compliance, and granular cost controls via batching and quant profiles."
[00:06:40] Priya: And pricing? Have a bracket ready.
[00:06:45] Lena: We should not quote exact, but give ranges. AE will follow up with detailed pricing. For demo say: 'usage-based hosted pricing, committed pricing for Dedicated, and custom for Private deployments.'
[00:07:00] Marco: Another common thing: people ask about model ownership vs serving. We say: "Competitive advantage is shifting from model ownership to serving — performance, cost, reliability matter."
[00:07:18] Sarah: Security dive: can you run through KMS and audit logs quickly?
[00:07:25] Marco: Yes. For Private we support customer-managed KMS/HSM and full audit logs; for Hosted we offer encryption at rest and customer keys for enterprise tiers. SSO via SAML/SCIM, RBAC, and long-term retention options.
[00:07:50] Sarah: Are you SOC2 or ISO certified?
[00:07:55] Lena: Yes, SOC2 Type II — we also have ISO in progress; offer to share the security appendix.
[00:08:05] Tom: What about data residency in EU?
[00:08:10] Marco: Regions and private deploys cover that — private VPC deployments for regulated workloads.
[00:08:22] [00:08:22] Marco: Back to demo: here's an embedding search example — show embeddings pipeline and rerank.
[00:08:38] Priya: When you show embeddings, flag the cost per unit and the option to cache vectors — customers like caching to save calls.
[00:08:50] Marco: We'll mention vector cache and partial reranking to reduce cost.
[00:09:05] Lena: Competitive note: when customers ask about latency vs cost tradeoffs, propose Dedicated for predictable latency and larger models, Hosted for quick start and lower operational overhead.
[00:09:24] Marco: Also mention Redwood Optimize: model/quantization recommendations and batching suggestions to lower unit cost.
[00:09:35] Sarah: How do we handle audits — can customers get logs for compliance demos?
[00:09:42] Lena: Yes we provide audit logs and can produce reports as part of enterprise onboarding.
[00:09:55] Marco: Alright let's run the timed 12-minute demo from top to bottom — I'll hit the main checkpoints and we'll time it.
[00:10:05] [00:10:05] Marco: Start timer. Intro (1m), platform tour (3m), streaming gen + warmed latency demo (2m), embeddings & rerank (2m), Dedicated/vs/private pitch (2m), security elevator (1m), closing + ask (1m).
[00:10:30] [00:11:00] Marco: (demo continues) show console logs -> show trace for a request -> highlight latency breakdown tokens / model compute / network.
[00:11:30] Tom: Suggestion: when you show traces, highlight token-level cost breakdowns — buyers love to see cost attribution.
[00:11:42] Marco: Good call. We'll show the token-cost pie and per-route analytics.
[00:11:55] Priya: For the ask, practice a clear next-step CTA: run a pilot or schedule a bench run with customer data.
[00:12:10] Marco: Good closure script: "We recommend a 4-week pilot with a small workload to validate latency and cost—we'll provide benchmarks and a dedicated SE during the pilot."
[00:12:25] Lena: roleplay: customer pushes on price — how do you respond?
[00:12:32] Marco: Offer committed pricing for Dedicated, and show Optimize wins to reduce unit costs; propose an initial proof-of-value with usage caps.
[00:12:45] Sarah: One tricky objection: "We can't send PII to hosted endpoints" — what's the quick answer?
[00:12:52] Marco: For regulated data, pitch Private (VPC/on-prem) or Dedicated with strict VPC peering and customer-managed keys. Offer to share compliance docs.
[00:13:10] Lena: We had a mispronunciation earlier, watch out for "KV cache" being said as "KV cash" — avoid that.
[00:13:20] Marco: noted.
[00:13:30] [00:13:30] Marco: Quick mock Q&A round — Lena will be the skeptical buyer.
[00:13:35] Lena: (seller voice) "If your Batch policy delays my customer's live chat responses, I'm not happy."
[00:13:45] Marco: "Our batching is workload-aware; we have latency SLOs and can configure per-route policies to bypass batching for low-latency routes. Also can use dedicated warm pools for critical endpoints."
[00:14:05] Lena: Good. Now competitive rebuttals: if buyer says 'we use Vertex AI', rebuttal?
[00:14:12] Marco: "Vertex is integrated in GCP but Redwood offers cross-cloud flexibility and model-agnostic serving with more operational controls and tuned inference kernels for latency/cost."
[00:14:30] Sarah: Customers often ask about model updates and rollouts — what's our story?
[00:14:36] Marco: Rollouts: canary, A/B tests, automatic fallbacks, pin versions—we've got rollouts and monitoring integrated.
[00:14:50] Priya: Make sure to mention observability: token-level cost, per-model dashboards, traces.
[00:14:58] Marco: yep. Also Redwood Console shows per-route dashboards and error analysis.
[00:15:10] [00:15:10] Lena: ok time check — we've used 15 mins. People are generally aligned. Let's confirm next steps and owners.
[00:15:22] Marco: action items recap: Marco will revise script and record cold/warm demo clip; Lena will publish battlecard and pricing ranges; schedule mock Q&A next week.
[00:15:40] Priya: ACK. Also Marco, include a slide with 'when to pick Dedicated vs Hosted vs Private' — a simple table.
[00:15:52] Marco: Will do.
[00:16:00] Tom: Small nit: when discussing KMS say 'customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM' — customers in finance will ask for HSM.
[00:16:09] Marco: added.
[00:16:20] Lena: Any other tough questions we want to rehearse?
[00:16:25] Marco: Maybe legal/procurement — we won't roleplay, but remember to surface procurement timelines: enterprise requires SOW, security review, and sometimes a dedicated cloud region.
[00:16:40] Lena: Great. Wrap up with concrete ask for SEs: internal enablement checklist — update demo, update battlecard, record latency clip, schedule mock customer run.
[00:16:55] Marco: I'll push the revised script to the enablement repo this week.
[00:17:05] Lena: I'll send the calendar invite for mock Q&A on 10/21 and share the security appendix.
[00:17:18] Sarah: Thanks everyone, that was useful.
[00:17:22] [00:17:22] END TRANSCRIPT (notes: some transcription errors present, e.g., 'cash' vs 'cache', product name slight mis-says).

References/links: demo deck link: short internal link (https://redwood.internal/decks/se-demo), security appendix link: (https://redwood.internal/security/appendix).

Recap / Next steps: Marco revise demo script + record clip; Lena distribute battlecard and schedule mock Q&A (10/21).
